scenario: [LSER.16.5.1]: two samples are one value exactly when `==` between them is `true`, so -0.0 and 0.0 are one value; [LSER.16.6.1] and [LSER.16.7.1] use the same equality. A `sliding 1_h` window absorbs 0.0, 1.0 and -0.0, one per pump; a fourth assert (9.0) reads the three before it ([LSER.8.6]). `count_distinct` is 2, `count_of(c.v, 0.0)` is 2 and `contains(c.v, -0.0)` is `true`, so each of the three rules logs, in source order. A bitwise equality gives 3, 1 and `true`, and the first two rules stay silent. PATH PINNED: libds `ds_series_ring_buffer_count_distinct` and the ring buffer's `query_with_value` (`series/ring_buffer.c`); Mercury `ds.series.aggregate` for `agg_count_distinct` (`sort_and_remove_dups` under the standard order) and `sample_matches`.
rules_ds:
use default

schema C scope logical:
    k: String key
    v: Float mutable

series C.v (by: k):
    count_distinct, count_of, contains sliding 1_h

rule distinct:
    C c where c.v > 5.0 and count_distinct(c.v) == 2
->
    log info "distinct"

rule counted:
    C c where c.v > 5.0 and count_of(c.v, 0.0) == 2
->
    log info "count_of"

rule found:
    C c where c.v > 5.0 and contains(c.v, -0.0)
->
    log info "contains"
